rules.statement: An external attribute that cannot be fetched never turns a Deny or Indeterminate into a Permit (P9'), except a DENY whose onMissing nomatch the control plane confirmed (ATR-6), which lapses by design.

An ALLOW skipped because an external attribute it reads cannot be fetched makes what would be the implicit deny Indeterminate (503); another matching ALLOW still permits, and onMissing nomatch makes it a plain miss.
A DENY may say onMissing nomatch only in the platform document, where it lapses while its attribute cannot be fetched; elsewhere the document does not compile.
A policy that reads an external attribute no registered AttributeProvider declares does not compile.
A provider that fails or times out makes only its own attributes unavailable; the other providers' attributes are still read, so their DENY still matches.
A DENY with onMissing nomatch compiles, in any document, only with the confirmation the control plane records (onMissingConfirmed); it then lapses while its attribute cannot be fetched.

A rate limit rule may say onMissing nomatch only in the platform document, where the rule does not count a request while its attribute cannot be fetched; in an app or tenant document it does not compile. Rate limit rules have no confirmation flow (ATR-6 covers policy statements).

An evaluation is decided on the external attributes it reads as their providers answer them, never refused because one was not fetched: the attribute plan holds every one it can read (the candidate statements' and their policies' conditions, the rate limit rules', and those of the boundary that holds the request's tenant, its statements' and its policy condition's), and the pipeline asks for each planned attribute the provider that declares it. A check (AuthorizationChecker) plans its own action and resource and asks stage-A and stage-B providers alike, whether or not a stage-B provider is registered. A boundary that does not hold the request is not planned.
